findings.claim: The publication preflight permits an explicit-table publication that already contains a local clinical command ledger.
findings.evidence: The preflight checked all-table and schema publications but did not inspect pg_publication_rel.
findings.suggested_fix: Check explicit membership and install a structural DDL guard against later additions.

findings.claim: An approved letter can be demoted to draft and thereby escape claim and document immutability controls.
findings.evidence: The approval trigger protected selected fields but omitted the status transition itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Make approval terminal except for the approved-to-signed transition.

findings.claim: A source mutation can race letter approval and commit after approval without being rejected.
findings.evidence: The source trigger used an unlocked status query while approval changed the letter independently.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize approval and source mutations through shared transaction locks.

findings.claim: Moving a QA result to another letter can remove QA evidence from an approved letter without checking the old letter.
findings.evidence: The UPDATE path selected only NEW.letter_id while DELETE selected OLD.letter_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Lock and validate both old and new letter IDs and update both revisions only when allowed.

findings.claim: Overlapping reassessments can erase the command ID needed to reconcile a later response-loss outcome.
findings.evidence: Every request overwrote one shared correlation and any success cleared it without command ownership.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow one pending mutation per scope or track pending commands separately.

findings.claim: Successful gate mutations and command lookups leave lastCommandId populated even though it represents uncertain outcomes only.
findings.evidence: The success paths updated gate state without clearing their matching correlation.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear only the matching correlation on definitive success and successful lookup.
